sources_note: One record per jurisdiction; source_url is the official regulator, statute or rule page used.

states.name: Alabama
states.regulator: Alabama Dept. of Finance, Division of Construction Management (Home Inspector Licensing)
states.field_training: Participate in 35 home inspections (or 100 inspections with the 35-hour education option); draft 25 reports, 10 reviewed by a qualified inspector
states.exam: NHIE plus ASHI Standards & Ethics exam
states.insurance: GL $20,000 property / $50,000 one person / $100,000 more than one person; E&O $250,000
states.ce: 15 hours per year
states.notes: Alternate path: 35 hours of education plus 100 inspections. Applicants also must qualify by membership (e.g., ASHI, InterNACHI), certification, Alabama trade licensure, or work experience.

states.name: Alaska
states.regulator: Alaska DCCED, Division of Corporations, Business & Professional Licensing - Home Inspectors
states.exam: NHIE, NAHI CRI or AHIT exam (existing homes); ICC residential inspector exams (new homes/joint)
states.ce: 8 contact hours per 2-year period (prorated at first renewal)
states.notes: State registration covers existing-home, new-home or joint categories; associate inspectors register under a supervising inspector. Application and renewal fees were not confirmed.

states.name: Arizona
states.regulator: Arizona State Board of Technical Registration
states.field_training: 30 parallel inspections with a qualified certified inspector
states.insurance: Financial assurance: E&O $100,000 per occurrence / $200,000 aggregate, or $25,000 bond or proof of $25,000 net assets
states.ce: None (per ASHI/InterNACHI; not confirmed on a Board page)
states.fees: Renewal $100 per year (Board fee table; not directly confirmed)
states.notes: Fingerprint clearance card required at application. Parallel inspectors must hold 3+ years of certification and 250+ Arizona inspections.

states.name: Arkansas
states.regulator: Arkansas State Board of Appraisers, Abstracters, and Home Inspectors (Home Inspector Registration Board)
states.field_training: 16 hours of field training included in the 80-hour qualifying education (64 instruction + 16 field)
states.exam: NHIE plus ASHI Standards of Practice & Code of Ethics exam
states.ce: 14 hours per year
states.notes: Qualifying education must be Board-approved and completed within 3 years before applying. The board now sits within the Department of Labor and Licensing.

states.name: California
states.notes: No state license. Business & Professions Code 7195-7199 sets a standard of care, bans conflicts of interest (e.g., repairs on inspected homes), and voids contract clauses that limit liability.

states.name: Colorado
states.notes: Colorado does not license or regulate home inspectors. Past licensing bills, such as 2015 SB 140, were not enacted.

states.name: Connecticut
states.regulator: Connecticut Dept. of Consumer Protection, Home Inspection Licensing Board
states.field_training: Intern permit plus 100 home inspections under a licensed inspector (first 10 under direct supervision)
states.exam: Written exam administered by DCP (passed NHIE scores accepted)
states.ce: 20 hours per 2-year cycle (includes 3 hours on current home inspection law)
states.renewal: Every 2 years (expires June 30 of odd years)
states.notes: The 40-hour Intern Training Program is set by Regs. 20-491-17. Regulations on inspection requirements and interns were updated effective November 1, 2023.

states.name: Delaware
states.regulator: Delaware Division of Professional Regulation, Board of Home Inspectors
states.field_training: 75 supervised home inspections (as registered trainee)
states.ce: 40 hours per 2-year period
states.notes: Training must be approved by ASHI or InterNACHI. Applicants must first register as a Delaware Home Inspector Trainee.

states.name: District of Columbia
states.notes: No District home inspector license was found. Businesses still need a DC Basic Business License from DLCP. No official page says outright that no license exists.

states.name: Florida
states.regulator: Florida DBPR, Home Inspectors
states.ce: 14 hours every 2 years (incl. 2 hours wind mitigation)
states.renewal: Every 2 years (expires July 31 of even years)
states.notes: Exams are given by nationally recognized providers approved by DBPR, not by the state.

states.name: Georgia
states.notes: No state license as of this check. SB 458, the Home Inspector Licensing Act, passed the Senate (Mar 6, 2026) and the House by substitute (Mar 31, 2026). Final enactment was not confirmed, and reported licensing start dates are 2027-2028.

states.name: Hawaii
states.notes: Hawaii has no state license. Licensing bills have been introduced before (e.g., SB 2403 in 2018) but none has been enacted.

states.name: Idaho
states.notes: Idaho does not license home inspectors. Wood-destroying-organism treatment recommendations fall under Idaho Dept. of Agriculture rules.

states.name: Illinois
states.regulator: Illinois Dept. of Financial & Professional Regulation (IDFPR), Division of Real Estate
states.field_training: Pre-license field course: 5 field inspection events plus a final field exam
states.exam: State licensing exam (via IDFPR testing vendor)
states.insurance: General liability $100,000 (kept 1 year after last report)
states.ce: 12 hours every 2 years (8 mandatory) for licensees first licensed on or before Aug 31, 2026
states.notes: P.A. 104-746 (eff. 7/31/2026) amended the Act and extended its sunset to Jan 1, 2032. Home inspector entities also need a license.

states.name: Indiana
states.regulator: Indiana Professional Licensing Agency, Home Inspectors Licensing Board
states.field_training: At least 12 hours of practical inspection experience within the 60-hour course
states.ce: 32 hours every 2 years
states.renewal: Every 2 years (by Oct 1 of odd years)
states.notes: The 60 hours must include at least 40 classroom hours (878 IAC). First-cycle CE is prorated.

states.name: Iowa
states.field_training: Qualifying association membership requires 100+ inspections
states.exam: Psychometric exam required for qualifying national association membership (not state-run)
states.insurance: E&O and GL each at least $100,000 per occurrence / $500,000 aggregate; max $2,500 deductible
states.ce: Via association membership (no state CE)
states.notes: Since July 1, 2025 (SF 460, Iowa Code 558A.4A), only these may issue home inspection reports: members of a qualifying national association or people they supervise, inspectors licensed in another state, licensed architects, and engineers. There is no state license or regulator.

states.name: Kansas
states.notes: Kansas has no state license; the former Home Inspectors Registration Act lapsed. HB 2709 (2026) would have required licensure and died. Real-estate pest (WDO) inspections need Dept. of Agriculture certification.

states.name: Kentucky
states.regulator: Kentucky Board of Home Inspectors (Kentucky Real Estate Authority, Public Protection Cabinet)
states.field_training: 16 of the 64 hours are field training (max 8 lab hours), plus 3 unpaid home inspections under direct supervision of a KY-licensed inspector
states.ce: 28 hours per biennial period (14 per license year), incl. 3 hrs KY law and 3 hrs report writing taken in person
states.renewal: Biennial license period per 831 KAR 2:040; renewal fee charged per year of licensure
states.fees: $250 application; $200 per year of licensure on renewal; $250 late renewal
states.notes: Requires state and FBI background checks. The regulations tie CE to odd/even renewal years; confirm the current renewal cycle with the board.

states.name: Louisiana
states.regulator: Louisiana State Board of Home Inspectors
states.field_training: Included in the 130: 90 hrs approved coursework, 30 hrs in-field platform training, and 10 live fee-paid inspections with a certified infield trainer
states.exam: NHIE (board-approved) plus the board's Standards of Practice/Code of Ethics exam and report-writing seminar
states.insurance: E&O min $300,000/yr and general liability min $300,000/yr, each with max $5,000 deductible
states.ce: 20 hours per year (30 hours for first renewal)
states.fees: $200 application; $100 renewal; $5 state fee per inspection, reported monthly
states.notes: Louisiana charges a $5 per-inspection state fee, with a monthly report due even when no inspections are done. Board rules are at LAC 46:XL.

states.name: Maine
states.notes: Maine has no statewide home inspector license; licensing bills (e.g., LD 168 in the 119th Legislature) have been proposed but none is in effect. Normal business registration applies.

states.name: Maryland
states.regulator: Maryland State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies and Home Inspectors (Maryland Department of Labor)
states.field_training: 72-hour course must be completed on-site (classroom), not virtually
states.ce: 30 hours per renewal (none for first renewal), incl. 2 hrs report writing and 2 hrs standards of practice
states.notes: Maryland adopted new Standards of Practice; the 2-hour standards-of-practice CE requirement is delayed until 1/1/2027.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.credential: License (Associate Home Inspector, then Home Inspector)
states.regulator: Massachusetts Board of Registration of Home Inspectors (Division of Occupational Licensure)
states.field_training: Associate: 25 inspections under direct supervision (up to 10 may be approved mock inspections). Full license: at least 1 year as associate plus 100 more supervised inspections
states.ce: 12 hours per 2-year cycle (incl. 4 hrs 266 CMR/SOP and 1 hr ethics)
states.renewal: Every 2 years (expires May 31 of even years)
states.fees: Associate $225; Home Inspector initial $338; renewal $225; late renewal $57
states.notes: Two-tier system: start as an Associate under a licensed supervisor, then upgrade after 1 year and 100 inspections. Fee figures come from mass.gov pages that blocked direct fetching.

states.name: Michigan
states.notes: Michigan has no statewide home inspector license; past licensing bills (e.g., 2021 HB 4500) did not pass, and no 2025-2026 licensing bill was found enacted.

states.name: Minnesota
states.notes: No statewide license. Some cities (Minneapolis, St. Paul, Maplewood and others) require a city-licensed Truth-in-Sale of Housing (TISH) evaluator for point-of-sale evaluations.

states.name: Mississippi
states.regulator: Mississippi Real Estate Appraisal Board, Mississippi Home Inspection Division (Home Inspector Regulatory Board)
states.field_training: 60-hour course may include field work as prescribed by the board
states.insurance: General liability min $250,000 and E&O min $250,000 per occurrence
states.ce: 20 hours every 2 years
states.fees: $175 application/exam; $325 license (initial and renewal); non-resident reciprocal application $50
states.notes: 2024 HB 1324 revived the Home Inspector Regulatory Board and moved oversight from the Real Estate Commission to the Real Estate Appraisal Board (effective July 1, 2024). Applicants must be 21; an optional New Home designation needs a builder license plus ICC certification.

states.name: Missouri
states.notes: No statewide license. 2026 HB 1832 would have created a Missouri Home Inspectors' Board, but it stalled in committee and did not become law.

states.name: Montana
states.regulator: Montana Department of Labor and Industry, Business Standards Division (Home Inspector Program)
states.insurance: E&O, minimum $125,000; must also keep membership in a national home inspection association
states.ce: None required by the state (national association CE rules may apply)
states.notes: New: HB 225 replaced business registration with an individual license effective Jan 1, 2026; active registrants were converted automatically. Renewal cycle not stated in the sources reviewed.

states.name: Nebraska
states.regulator: Nebraska Secretary of State, Licensing Division
states.notes: Registration only, with no education or exam requirement, in effect since Jan 1, 2023 (LB 423, 2021). Inspectors must register before inspecting and list any national certification held.

states.name: Nevada
states.regulator: Nevada Real Estate Division (Inspectors of Structures)
states.field_training: Observe 25 fee-paid inspections by a certified general/master inspector or approved instructor
states.exam: State-approved Inspector of Structures exam (NHIE-based, via Pearson VUE)
states.insurance: E&O min $100,000 and general liability min $100,000
states.ce: 20 hours per 2-year renewal (incl. 3 hrs safety, 2 hrs NRS/NAC 645D)
states.fees: NRS: $100 application + $250 issuance/renewal + $15 technology fee; Division lists $365 for initial residential certificate; exam $100
states.notes: Nevada certifies residential, general and master inspectors; the general and master tiers need more hours and inspections.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.regulator: New Hampshire Board of Home Inspectors (Office of Professional Licensure and Certification)
states.insurance: Proof of liability insurance required; rules do not set a minimum amount
states.ce: 20 hours per 2-year renewal period
states.fees: $200 biennial renewal; application fee not confirmed from official page
states.notes: No minimum field-inspection count. Criminal background check required.

states.name: New Jersey
states.regulator: New Jersey Home Inspection Advisory Committee (Division of Consumer Affairs)
states.field_training: At least 40 hours of unpaid field-based inspections under a licensed inspector (part of the 180); alternative path: 250 fee-paid supervised inspections
states.ce: 40 hours every 2 years
states.notes: Current fee schedule not confirmed (a 2006 rule listed $125 application and $500 initial license). The associate inspector class was eliminated in 2005.

states.name: New Mexico
states.regulator: New Mexico Regulation and Licensing Department, Home Inspectors Board
states.field_training: 80 hours of field training including at least 30 parallel inspections
states.insurance: E&O min $250,000 aggregate and professional liability min $250,000
states.ce: 60 hours per 3-year license (incl. 6 hrs ethics)
states.notes: The 80 classroom hours may be taken online. Other routes exist by experience or by out-of-state credentials. Board rules were updated in April 2024.

states.name: New York
states.regulator: New York Department of State, Division of Licensing Services
states.field_training: 40 of the 140 hours are unpaid field-based inspections under a licensed inspector, PE or architect; alternative: 100 supervised inspections
states.exam: NYS home inspector exam or NHIE
states.ce: 24 hours every 2 years
states.notes: Applicants need a high school diploma or equivalent and must have no disqualifying criminal convictions.

states.name: North Carolina
states.regulator: North Carolina Home Inspector Licensure Board (Office of State Fire Marshal)
states.field_training: Included in the 200: at least 120 hrs classroom plus at least 80 hrs field instruction with at least 10 site visits
states.insurance: General liability $250,000 plus one of: E&O $250,000, a surety bond (min $5,000), or $5,000-$10,000 net assets
states.ce: 12 hours per year (16 per year for the first 3 years for some new licensees)
states.fees: $35 application; $80 exam; $160 license issuance/renewal; $30 late renewal
states.notes: Board rules were amended effective June 1, 2026; licensees must file a general liability certificate each January naming the Board as holder. GCs, architects and PEs licensed 6+ months may qualify without the course.

states.name: North Dakota
states.regulator: North Dakota Secretary of State - Licensing
states.exam: Home inspection exam from ASHI, InterNACHI, EBPHI (NHIE) or ICC
states.insurance: E&O coverage of $100,000 or more (liability certificate)
states.ce: None listed
states.notes: Registration under NDCC ch. 43-54 is mandatory before inspecting for pay. No set pre-licensing hours; the Secretary of State page lists no CE requirement.

states.name: Ohio
states.regulator: Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of Real Estate & Professional Licensing (Ohio Home Inspector Board)
states.field_training: 10 parallel inspections with a licensed Ohio inspector, or a board-approved experience curriculum plus one peer review
states.insurance: Commercial/comprehensive general liability; $100,000 per occurrence / $300,000 aggregate (per InterNACHI summary of rule)
states.ce: 14 hours per year (42 hours per 3-year term)
states.notes: Fingerprint background check required. HB 59 (136th GA, occupational-regulation streamlining) passed the House and was pending in a Senate committee in 2026; it amends ORC 4764, so watch for changes.

states.name: Oklahoma
states.regulator: Oklahoma Construction Industries Board (CIB), Committee of Home Inspector Examiners
states.insurance: General liability, at least $50,000 combined single limit
states.ce: 8 hours per year (max 2 hours ancillary systems)
states.notes: A CIB 2027 rule impact statement proposes fee changes for Chapter 70, so fees may rise. Reciprocity licensing is available.

states.name: Oregon
states.regulator: Oregon Construction Contractors Board (CCB)
states.field_training: Points system: 20 education points; ride-along inspections under an Oregon certified inspector count 1 point each; work experience can substitute
states.insurance: Business must hold a CCB license with Home Inspector Services endorsement: $15,000 bond and $100,000 per-occurrence liability insurance
states.ce: 30 hours every 2 years
states.fees: Certification $150 (2 years); renewal $150; NHIE $225; CCB business license fee separate
states.notes: Two layers: the individual certification plus a CCB-licensed business the inspector owns or works for. Education is measured in points (OAR 812-008-0040), not hours.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.field_training: Full membership in a national home inspection association requires more than 100 inspections; non-full members must be supervised by a full member who signs the report
states.exam: Recognized or accredited exam required for full association membership
states.insurance: Professional liability (E&O) and general liability, $100,000 per occurrence / $500,000 aggregate; deductible max $2,500
states.notes: No state license or board. The Home Inspection Law (68 Pa.C.S. ch. 75) requires inspectors to be full members of a national association (or supervised by one), or licensed engineers/architects, and to carry insurance; it is enforced through consumer protection law.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.credential: Home Inspector license (Associate Home Inspector tier)
states.regulator: Rhode Island Contractors' Registration and Licensing Board (CRLB)
states.field_training: 1 year as a licensed associate home inspector plus 100 paid inspections (or 5 years as a licensed contractor)
states.ce: 12 hours every 2 years (incl. 1 hr ethics, 1 hr standards of practice)
states.notes: Associate home inspectors work under a licensed inspector's direct supervision. Licensing has been mandatory since January 1, 2020.

states.name: South Carolina
states.regulator: SC LLR - Residential Builders Commission
states.field_training: 1 year supervised experience OR a Commission-approved formal home inspection course (by-exam route); 50 inspections is an option for the without-exam route
states.exam: SC Home Inspector technical exam or NHIE, plus SC Business Management & Law exam (PSI)
states.renewal: Every 2 years, by June 30 of even years
states.notes: Course length is set by the approved provider; InterNACHI cites 120 hours and says no CE is required, but neither figure appears on LLR pages. Statute text says annual renewal while LLR says biennial.

states.name: South Dakota
states.credential: Registered Home Inspector / Licensed Home Inspector
states.regulator: South Dakota Real Estate Commission (Dept. of Labor & Regulation)
states.field_training: None for registration; Licensed tier requires 1 year as registered inspector and 100 paid inspections
states.exam: State home inspector exam via PSI (75% to pass)
states.insurance: None found in statute or rules
states.ce: 24 hours per renewal (max 6 hours independent study)
states.renewal: Every 2 years (expires Dec 31 of year after issuance)
states.notes: Two tiers with the same duties: start as Registered, then upgrade to Licensed with an experience log.

states.name: Tennessee
states.regulator: Tennessee Dept. of Commerce & Insurance - Home Inspector Licensing Program
states.insurance: General liability at least $500,000 plus E&O (no minimum stated); State of Tennessee named as certificate holder
states.ce: 32 hours every 2 years
states.notes: Rule chapter 0780-05-12 was amended effective January 22, 2026. Out-of-state licensees may substitute 32 TN-approved CE hours for the 90-hour course.

states.name: Texas
states.regulator: Texas Real Estate Commission (TREC)
states.field_training: Substitute path: 40-hour Texas Practicum (within the 194 hours). Sponsored path: 12 months as a licensed Real Estate Inspector, 175 inspections, 134 hours
states.exam: State exam (national + state portions, Pearson VUE)
states.insurance: Professional liability (or other coverage) of $100,000 per occurrence; TREC certificate of insurance
states.ce: 32 hours every 2 years (incl. 8-hour Legal & Ethics and SOP Review)
states.fees: Original application $120 + $4 online fee; renewal $60 + $4 (fee schedule effective Sept 1, 2026); exam fees paid to Pearson VUE
states.notes: Three tiers: Apprentice Inspector, Real Estate Inspector (both sponsored by a Professional Inspector) and Professional Inspector. Fingerprints with Texas DPS are required; applications go through TREC's REALM Portal.

states.name: Utah
states.regulator: Utah Division of Professional Licensing (DOPL)
states.exam: Certification from ASHI, InterNACHI or ICC (Residential Combination Inspector); no separate state exam named
states.insurance: General liability and E&O, each at least $500,000; DOPL named as certificate holder
states.notes: New license created by HB 58 (2025); DOPL opened applications and began enforcement May 1, 2026. Utah previously had no home inspector license, and DOPL has not yet posted fees, renewal cycle or CE.

states.name: Vermont
states.regulator: Vermont Secretary of State, Office of Professional Regulation (OPR)
states.ce: None required
states.notes: Licensed under 26 V.S.A. ch. 19; fees are set in 3 V.S.A. section 125 and could not be confirmed (OPR pages blocked automated access).

states.name: Virginia
states.credential: License (Home Inspector); optional New Residential Structure (NRS) specialty
states.regulator: Virginia DPOR - Board for Asbestos, Lead, and Home Inspectors
states.field_training: 15 qualifying points total, at least 5 from education and 5 from experience (each 5 inspections = 1 point; full-time months = 2 points)
states.insurance: No insurance requirement found in regulations
states.ce: 16 hours per 2-year cycle (NRS holders: 4 of these on NRS topics)
states.notes: 35 hours is the minimum course (5 points); the 70-hour course earns 10 points. An NRS specialty is required to inspect new homes.

states.name: Washington
states.regulator: Washington State Department of Licensing (Home Inspector Advisory Licensing Board)
states.field_training: 40 hours of field training, including 5 inspections, with an inspector licensed 4+ years
states.ce: 24 hours every 2 years
states.notes: Out-of-state inspectors licensed 2 of the last 4 years take only the state portion of the exam.

states.name: West Virginia
states.regulator: West Virginia State Fire Marshal's Office - Regulatory & Licensing Division
states.ce: 16 hours per year (per InterNACHI/ASHI; not confirmed in rule)
states.notes: Governed by Legislative Rule Title 103, Series 7 (replaced 87 CSR 5). WV and FBI fingerprint checks, a high school diploma or GED, and a WV business license are required.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.regulator: Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services (DSPS)
states.field_training: At least 20 of the 40 hours must be hands-on inspection and report-writing training
states.exam: NHIE plus Wisconsin statutes & rules exam (85% to pass)
states.ce: 40 hours every 2 years (not required before the second renewal)
states.fees: Credential $55; state law exam $75 (per DSPS form 2466, not re-confirmed)
states.notes: The 40-hour pre-registration requirement comes from 2021 Act 17 (SPS 131.40/131.405, permanent from July 1, 2023). The credential is called a registration but is required, with exams.

states.name: Wyoming
states.notes: No statewide home inspector license, so inspectors need only normal business registration. Local rules may apply, and many hold voluntary InterNACHI or ASHI certification.
